The fitted item profiles of an lca() fit

Source: R/lca.R
lca_profiles.Rd

The class-conditional item-response probabilities pi[j, c, k], which are the main output of a latent class analysis: for each item, a K x C_j table of the probability of each category given each class. This is poLCA's $probs.

Usage

lca_profiles(fit)

Arguments

fit

A frmtmb_fit with an lca() family.

Value

A named list with one K x C_j probability matrix per item, of class frmtmb_lca_profiles, carrying the estimated class sizes (the mean prior class probabilities, poLCA's $P) in the class_sizes attribute.

See also

lca(), lca_probs()

Examples

set.seed(2)
n <- 200
cl <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5) + 1
pr <- rbind(c(0.9, 0.85, 0.8), c(0.1, 0.15, 0.2))
Y <- matrix(0L, n, 3)
for (j in 1:3) Y[, j] <- 1L + rbinom(n, 1, pr[cl, j])
dd <- data.frame(row = seq_len(n))
dd$Y <- Y
fit <- frm(bf(Y ~ 1), family = lca(K = 2), data = dd)

pf <- lca_profiles(fit)
pf
#> <lca profiles> 2 classes, 3 items
#> 
#> Estimated class sizes (mean prior probability):
#> class1 class2 
#>  0.437  0.563 
#> 
#> item1:
#>          cat1   cat2
#> class1 0.9465 0.0535
#> class2 0.1179 0.8821
#> 
#> item2:
#>          cat1   cat2
#> class1 0.8745 0.1255
#> class2 0.2005 0.7995
#> 
#> item3:
#>          cat1   cat2
#> class1 0.8209 0.1791
#> class2 0.2332 0.7668
pf[[1]]                       # item 1's K x C table
#>             cat1       cat2
#> class1 0.9464869 0.05351314
#> class2 0.1179051 0.88209491
attr(pf, "class_sizes")
#>    class1    class2 
#> 0.4370062 0.5629938
